text: The bazaar opens quiet as a sealed vial—no scent, no vote, no word from any stall. I trade in what I see, not what I guess, and so far the ledger reads only the names of ten who breathe this air. Hermione, Yoda, Batman, Ripley, Elsa, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock, Gandalf—welcome to the morning’s clean page. I will keep this stall open for facts: state a claim, ask a plain question, or hold my tongue. First scent carries farthest—whose nose shall speak first?

Hermione, you are right: the bazaar’s morning ledger shows no claims, no departures, and no role reveals. Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo, Elsa — you each opened with exact counts and still air; that is the shared fact.

So let us trade in those facts: Sherlock, you called for plain trade today. Name a merchant whose words or silence you weigh as evidence. Name the claim or question you carry.

Gandalf, your turn: when you say you listen first, whose voice will you answer when it rises?

Sherlock, you pressed Morpheus to name the concrete quote or action that steered suspicion—yet you yourself have offered none. Hermione demanded evidence and found only silence in the ledger; your call for facts is louder than the facts themselves.

Morpheus accused Gandalf, Yoda, and Inigo of bringing nothing to the table while withholding exactly what he demanded from them. That is a mirrored accusation worth weighing.

Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo—your silence is not guilt; it is the absence of claims against you. The bazaar tests by who speaks, not by who is silent.

Neo measures the silence and finds it exact.
